etymologies.etymologyHTML: From realist +‎ -ic.

definitions.definition: Expressed or represented as being accurate, practicable, or not idealistic.

quote.citation: 2011 October 1, Tom Fordyce, “Rugby World Cup 2011: England 16-12 Scotland”, in BBC Sport‎[1]:
quote.text: Scotland needed a victory by eight points to have a realistic chance of progressing to the knock-out stages, and for long periods of a ferocious contest looked as if they might pull it off.

definitions.definition: Relating to the representation of objects, actions or conditions as they actually are or were.
